Subject: Inference delivery options — hosted vs reserved vs private (post-call recap)

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and the handful of asks we agreed on so we can move pricing/contracting forward.

Summary of BrightLeaf requirements (what I heard)
- Typical monthly usage: ~3.2M generated tokens (textgen + chat), mostly business-hours but 2–3x bursts for campaigns.
- Target p95 latency: <= 200ms per token for interactive flows.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 required, customer data must remain within US regions; potential to evaluate VPC/private deployment for limited PII workloads.
- Timeline: pilot in December, procurement decision in Jan.

High-level economics (illustrative):
- Hosted API (no commit): $0.0008 / token -> ~ $2,560 / month @ 3.2M tokens. Fastest to start, includes model updates and monitoring.
- Dedicated (reserved commit): example reserved pool (8xA10-equivalent) ~ $18,000 / month -> effective cost ~ $0.0005 / token at 40M token capacity; break-even vs hosted at ~6.4M tokens/month. Dedicated gives isolation, predictable throughput, and lower per-token cost at scale.
- Private VPC / on-prem: higher up-front integration and support; we typically model a 3–6 month ramp and a platform license + infra OPEX. Good for strict data residency and HSM/KMS integration.

Concrete asks / next steps
1) Confirm that 3.2M tokens/month is the right central estimate and share per-flow splits (interactive vs batch).
2) Confirm whether the VPC/on-prem option is a firm requirement for production or if a hybrid approach (hosted for general traffic + VPC for PII) is acceptable.
3) If budget holder consent exists, confirm target monthly budget band for inference (ballpark).
4) I'll share a modeled cost spreadsheet and a draft SOW for a hosted pilot with optional reserved evaluation.

Attached: capacity_estimates.xlsx (rough math) — this is an initial model, will iterate after you confirm traffic split.

I'll follow up with a short pricing grid and two recommended pilot paths by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Dylan Brooks

Emma — great context, thanks. Quick answers then a compact cost sketch and burst handling details.

Burst handling
- Hosted API: automatic elastic capacity across our multi-tenant pool; bursts are absorbed until rate limits are reached. We offer short-term burst credits for unexpected spikes (subject to fair-use). If you expect repeated campaign spikes (9–10M), we'd recommend a short dedicated burst reservation during campaign windows or a temporary scale-up of a dedicated pool.
- Dedicated (reserved): you get guaranteed GPU capacity; we also allow configured burst pools (paid add-on) to handle episodic traffic beyond committed throughput. No throttling until you hit the pool's max RPS; beyond that we can queue or fail depending on policy.

Simplified cost math (illustrative)
Assumptions: 3.2M steady tokens, 2 campaign spikes/quarter each ~8M tokens sustained for 48h.
- Hosted (no commit): $0.0008/token -> steady month cost = 3.2M * 0.0008 = $2,560. Campaign months (with spikes) could go to ~ $8–9k depending on total tokens.
- Dedicated reserved example: $18,000/month commitment -> supports peak capacity comfortably; amortized per-token if you consume 40M tokens = $0.00045/token. Break-even point vs hosted (0.0008/token) is at ~6.4M tokens/month.
- Hybrid pilot option: 3-month hosted pilot with a scoped dedicated trial for one campaign window. We can apply a 25% credit toward first-month dedicated commitment if you convert after pilot.

Next steps I recommend:
1) You confirm traffic split (interactive vs batch). I'll update the attached capacity_estimates.xlsx with per-flow rows and a month-by-month ramp.
2) If pilot sounds good, Marissa will draft a one-page SOW for a 3-month hosted pilot + optional dedicated evaluation for the first campaign.
3) Karthik can follow on the technical integration (VPC/KMS checklist) and provide an ETA for a VPC proof-of-concept.

I've summarized the above in the attached SOW draft and updated the spreadsheet with the campaign spike scenario. Open to scheduling a 30-min cost walk-through.

—Dylan
